newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo Trepca, Greek Mitileneos sign $519 mln deal.
newsitem.headline: Yugo Trepca, Greek Mitileneos sign $519 mln deal.

text.p: Yugoslavia's Rudarsko Metalurski Kombinat Trepca metal works and the leading Greek metals trading firm Mitileneos have signed a five-year cooperation deal worth $519 million, the Belgrade daily Politika said on Tuesday.

The deal was signed on Monday in the Greek economy ministry and the signing ceremony was attended by Yugoslav Finance Minister Bozidar Gazivoda, President of the Yugoslav Chamber of Commerce Mihajlo Milojevic and general managers of Trepca, Yugoslav foreign trade firm Generalexport and Jugobanka.
Trepca will supply its Greek partner with lead and zinc metal worth $350 million over the next five years.
In turn, Mitileneos will provide Trepca with lead and zinc concentrate worth $150 million and mining equipment and spare parts worth $19 million, Politika said.

"The deal is the result of an almost two-year cooperation with Mitileneos commenced under very difficult conditions when Trepca was launching its rehabilitation programme," Trepca managing director Novak Bjelic was quoted as saying.
"The new agreement is the basis not only of five-year but of more long-term cooperation," said Bjelic.
Trepca's first deals with Mitilineos, worth $2 million, were signed in 1995, the paper said.
The Trepca group, based in Serbia's southern province of Kosovo, includes 14 lead and zinc mines and several factories.
